seoDescription: Learn how to use a curling iron with this step-by-step tutorial for beginners. This guide covers everything from choosing the right tool—exploring barrel size, length, and temperature settings—to prepping your hair with heat protectant. Master the fundamental technique of curling from root to tip, controlling the curl direction, and avoiding common mistakes like kinks. Follow along to learn how to section hair properly, finish your style with the right products, and achieve beautiful, lasting curls or waves.

summary:
## Key Concepts for Curling Iron Beginners

### Choosing the Right Tool

- **Curling Iron vs. Wand**: A **curling iron** has a **clip**, which is essential for the techniques shown. A curling wand does not have a clip.
- **Barrel Size**: Determines the tightness of the curl. A **1.25 inch** barrel is recommended for its versatility, allowing for both loose waves and tighter ringlets.
- **Barrel Length**: Choose a length that matches your hair. Longer hair benefits from a longer barrel for more "real estate."
- **Temperature Settings**: An adjustable temperature is a **must-have**. A good starting point is **350-365°F (175-185°C)**. Use lower heat for damaged or bleached hair and higher heat for coarse, thick hair.

### Preparation and Practice

> [!IMPORTANT]
> For absolute beginners, practice every step with a **cold, unplugged curling iron**. This builds muscle memory for twisting your wrist and using the clip without any risk. Use a mirror to watch your movements.

1.  **Heat Protectant**: Always apply a **heat protectant** and brush it through to ensure even distribution and prevent heat spots.
2.  **Sectioning**: Section your hair for the best results. A good first section is from just above the ears downwards.

### The Core Curling Technique

- **Start at the Root**: For the most consistent, defined curl, always start near the **root** and work your way down. Starting at the ends leads to uneven heat distribution.
- **Use the Clip**: The clip is your guide. The proper technique involves clamping a section of hair, twisting the barrel, slightly opening the clip to slide the iron down the hair, and repeating.
- **Curl Direction**: The position of the clip dictates the curl's direction. To curl away from the face, the clip should be on top of the hair section, guiding the barrel away.

> [!NOTE]
> Your curling iron will tell you if you're doing it wrong. If you feel tension or the hair starts to form a **kink**, your clip is likely in the wrong position for your desired curl direction. Stop and reposition.

### Finishing and Styling

> [!TIP]
> Let your curls **cool completely** before touching them. This is the most critical step for making your style last.

- Once cool, you can use your fingers, a **wide-tooth comb** (for separated curls), or a hairbrush (for a very soft wave) to style the hair.
- Apply finishing products like **hairspray**, **texture spray**, or **dry shampoo** to add hold and grit, especially for fine hair.

## Choosing Your Curling Iron

How to use a curling iron for beginners. Personally, it's one of my favorite hair styling tools because of the versatility. Let's go together with a step-by-step guide on how to curl your hair. 

What is a curling iron? The curling iron has the clip, but the curling wand has nothing. I think there are three things when looking at a curling iron that are very important. Number one is the size of the barrel. Number two is the length of the barrel. And number three, does it offer temperature settings?

Starting with the size of the barrel, that's pretty much how thick the barrel is. In my opinion, the optimum size is 1 and a/4 in. So 1.25 in. The reason why is I find that it has the most versatility to what type of curl or waves you want to achieve. You can do a very light bend or you can do a nice tight ringlet with 1.25 in. But again, those are all little techniques.

The next thing, the length of the barrel. So there are different lengths. Yes, here you go. Just look at the difference. You have a long extra long barrel versus like a traditional size and then something in between. So I think depending on your hair length and your hair needs, I would go for something a little bit more traditional or if you have very long hair, I would go for something like this, very long. That way you have a ton of real estate for your hair sections.

Now let's talk about the curling iron temperature. I think it's a must for beginners to play around with the temperature settings for your hair needs. So, the optimum temperature setting in my opinion for so many other hair tools as well, they think it's 365° F. For me personally, I stick around 350 to 365, but again, it depends on what my hair is at that state. For example, if it's very bleached, I will go lower because my hair is damaged and it does not need that high of a heat temperature. But if your hair is coarse and it's thick and it can handle the heat, definitely go higher than 365 and play around with the hair temperature setting for your curling iron.

## Hair Prep & Beginner Practice

Now that we got that out of the way, let's get into the visual tutorial of how to use a curling iron. 

Step one, add your favorite heat protectant. I'm just going to brush it through. Make sure I don't have any knots and also the heat protectant is distributed through my hair. And the reason why they recommend to use a heat protectant is to make sure there are no heat spots on your hair when you're using a heat tool.

I personally like to section my hair to get the best results. I like to start right above my ears. Clip it back. Pin it back. 

If you're a very beginner, like you've never used a curling iron before, please practice all of these steps with a cold turned off curling iron. The reason why is you're going to get into your muscle memory and also have a mirror in front of you. That way you can see exactly what you're doing, the way you're holding it, and understand like where the clip is, why the clip is doing what it's doing, how you need to maneuver your wrist, twist your wrist, and etc. That's what I did for a long time to understand how do I twist it? Why is it twisting that way? Why is why am I getting kinks in my hair? And that way you'll be able to use a curling iron like a professional. 

Today I'm going to use the Babyliss Pro curling iron. This is the 1.25 in. Again, it's just one of my favorite sizes for the versatility in my opinion.

## The Core Curling Technique

We're going to go to let's go like 360. So now you're going to grab a section of hair. So, if you grab a thicker section, it's going to be more of a loose wave or even a slight bend in your hair. Now, if you grab a smaller section, it's going to be a little bit more defined. There's going to be a little bit more curl and it's not going to be as loose. 

You grab a section of hair, you put it on the barrel. The clip is at the top. Again, I'm always using the clip. You give a little twist. Clip. Little twist. Clip. Twist. Open up the clip. You see how I'm always using the clip? And this is where you decide how much hair you want to be outside of the clip, like not in the barrel. You hold it there for a couple of seconds and then the best and easiest way you just slide it out. And always the very end using the clip. 

So now going to the left side, the clip is going to be basically on the opposite. If I'm going towards my face, which I want to go towards my face, the clip is going to be on underneath my hair. The section of hair, it's not going to be at the top. It's going to be underneath. So, grab the hair and I'm kind of going, I'm not going just down like this. I'm kind of going at an angle the way my hair is laying in the barrel. So, again, using the clip, always have it in your finger. Twist. Take the clip and hold it open a little bit. Twist it back up. And I'm just going with the length of the section of my hair. Clip open, closed, and now it's standing there. Hold it there for a couple of seconds. And then just gently slide down. And then with the clip, you gently just slide the hair out. That way, it's nice and sleek and it's smooth at the bottom.

## Why & How to Curl from the Root

This is going towards my face. There are no kinks. And the reason why I like to start at the root, it just gives the most defined and consistent curl or wave. If you start at the bottom with the with the ends and basically roll your way up to the roots, the heat distribution is very uneven and the top of the hair is going to be sitting on top of the other hair and it's not going to get the heat that you want. 

So now I'm going to go away from my face and this is on the left side. So I'm putting the hair through the clip and the barrel. And you see how the clip is on top of my hair now. That's going to basically move the barrel away from my face, the curling iron. So, using the clip, opening it up. Do a little twist. Use my thumb. Open it up ever so slightly. Move it back up. And move it back up. Hold it there again for, you know, depending on your hair type. And this is where you're going to practice and find out what your hair needs. Slide. And then use the clip. Slide down.

## Sectioning & Troubleshooting Kinks

Bottom section is done. Let's create a new section of hair. Now, this time I'm going to go right up to my temples. Again, it depends on the length and the thickness of your hair. This is kind of where you're also going to play around with what you're trying to achieve. Sometimes I only do two sections. Sometime I don't section my hair. I just start from the very back and just work my way forward. 

Now, I want to show you guys. Let's say I want to go towards my face and I use the clip wrong or it's positioned wrong. So, if I want to go towards my face, you're going to look in the mirror and you're like, "Okay, the clip is now above the section of hair and it's working. It's not going against me. And this is why practicing with a cold curling iron really helps in my opinion.

So now I'm on the left side and I want the curl going towards my face. Watch the clip. If I want to go towards, see how it's not letting me? There's a kink right away. That means I'm holding it wrong. And you'll actually feel the tension a little bit. So now look at the clip. See how it's underneath and the barrel is on top of the section? Right away you'll be like, "Oh, okay. Yep. That's the correct way."

Slide down. Slide down. And gently. I'm just going one more time. And I'm basically leaving off the mohawk at the very top. If you're still not really understanding like how the direction is supposed to go, like where the clip is supposed to sit, literally take the section of hair on a cold curling iron and practice that way. Like holding the clip, opening the clip, twisting your hair up, twisting your hair down, sliding your barrel through your hair, and so forth. I promise you practicing with a cold curling iron all these little techniques, you will understand exactly what you're supposed to do when you're looking at yourself in the mirror.

## Finishing the Top & Final Curls

And once you're ready, turn that bad boy up. You're good to go. And this is where you're going to create your parting line of where you want your hair to sit. And the same thing, just go in the back and just bring the hair forward. So, I'm just going to roll it up about there. Roll it down a little bit more. Stop. Stop and hold. And then gently unwind. Slide down. Slide down. And now don't forget to turn off your curling iron. I know. I know I have to say this, but please turn it off and take it out out of your outlet.

## Setting and Styling Your Curls

Before I do anything else, I'm going to let the curls really cool and set. And you can feel by just touching your hair. If it still feels warm to the touch, just let it go. just don't do anything. 

So, you either can leave your hair like this, you can add some hairspray, you can add some hair texturing spray, dry shampoo. If your hair is really fine and silky, you need to add some texture to it. But if you don't, you can just use your fingers to comb it out or you can just leave it like this. It's a personal preference. In my opinion, for my hair type and for what I like out of my hairstyle, I like using a wide tooth comb. Or if you really want to brush it out, just use a regular hair brush and really comb out and brush out your hair to give it more of that soft wave, soft bend. 

And there you go. You've mastered and how to curl your hair using a curling iron. I really hope this how to use a curling iron for beginners helped you. I hope it answered most or all of your questions of how to use a curling iron, why you should do certain things, why you shouldn't do the other things, and so forth. But thank you guys so much for watching. I hope you have a wonderful time exploring your curling iron and really figuring out what you want and what your hair wants. But for now, thank you so much for watching, spending time with me, and I'll see the next one very soon. Bye.
